module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 966

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/966](https://www.erdosproblems.com/966)
- [Er75b] Erdős, Paul, *Problems and results in combinatorial number theory*. Journées
  Arithmétiques de Bordeaux (Conf., Univ. Bordeaux, Bordeaux, 1974) (1975), 295-310.
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace Erdos966

/--
Let $k,r\geq 2$. Does there exist a set $A\subseteq \mathbb{N}$ that contains no non-trivial
arithmetic progression of length $k+1$, yet in any $r$-colouring of $A$ there must exist a
monochromatic non-trivial arithmetic progression of length $k$?

Erdős [Er75b] reported that 'Spencer has recently shown that such a sequence exists', but gives
no reference.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 11, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/main/src/v4.29.1/ErdosProblems/Erdos966.lean"]
theorem erdos_966 : answer(True) ↔
    ∀ k r : ℕ, 2 ≤ k → 2 ≤ r → ∃ A : Set ℕ, A.IsAPOfLengthFree (k + 1) ∧
      ∀ coloring : A → Fin r, ContainsMonoAPofLength coloring k := by
  sorry

end Erdos966

reformulations.difference: The source's 'no non-trivial AP of length k+1' and 'monochromatic non-trivial AP of length k' are expressed through the repository predicates `Set.IsAPOfLengthFree (↑k + 1)` (no subset t ⊆ A with `t.IsAPOfLength (k+1)`, i.e. `ENat.card t = k+1 ∧ t = {a + n•d | n < k+1}`) and `ContainsMonoAPofLength coloring k` (a set of elements of ↥A, all of one colour, whose image in ℕ is `IsAPOfLength k`). Non-triviality (d ≠ 0) is never written explicitly; it is forced by the cardinality condition. Colourings are functions `↥A → Fin r`; A ⊆ ℕ may contain 0 and may be finite, whereas Erdős's original [Er75b] speaks of a 'sequence' split into r subsequences.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Proved in Lean (sorry-free scratch file on the repository toolchain): for k ≥ 1, `A.IsAPOfLengthFree (↑k+1) ↔ ¬∃ a d, d ≠ 0 ∧ ∀ i < k+1, a+i*d ∈ A`; for k ≥ 2, `ContainsMonoAPofLength coloring k ↔ ∃ c a d, d ≠ 0 ∧ ∀ i < k, ∃ h : a+i*d ∈ A, coloring ⟨_, h⟩ = c`. A set of cardinality k ≥ 2 of the form {a+nd} forces d ≠ 0, and n ↦ a+nd is injective for d ≠ 0. From these I proved the whole right-hand side equivalent to the explicit formulation with colourings ℕ → Fin r and d ≠ 0 (extend a colouring of A by a default colour, possible since r ≥ 2; restrict a colouring of ℕ to A). That explicit formulation is the statement of the linked plby proof. The remaining points are immaterial and argued on paper, not in Lean. (1) 0 ∈ ℕ: translate. (2) Finite vs infinite A: given a finite example B with M = max B + 1, the union of the blocks 2M·3^j + B (j ≥ 0) is infinite. Every 3-term AP x<y<z in it lies in one block: if z is in a later block than y then z > 2y, forcing x < 0; then y−x = z−y < M keeps x in the same block. So the union is still (k+1)-AP-free (k+1 ≥ 3), and every r-colouring has a monochromatic k-AP in the first block. (3) 'Split into r subsequences' is an r-colouring.

review.notes: No defects found. The docstring matches the erdosproblems.com LaTeX source word for word, and Erdős's original wording in Astérisque 24-25 (1975), §IV(i), poses the same claim ('property A(k)' = contains a k-term AP). Status is consistent: erdosproblems.com shows 'PROVED (LEAN) — solved in the affirmative', matching `research solved`, `answer(True)` and the `formal_proof using lean4` link. The linked plby/Aristotle proof (Hales–Jewett applied to the base-2k image of [k]^n) compiles unchanged on this repository's toolchain (Lean v4.33.1). Combined with my sorry-free equivalence lemmas, it proves a theorem whose type is exactly `type_of% @Erdos966.erdos_966` (checked with `rfl`); a deliberately false `example` confirmed the error reporting works. The k = 2 case is trivial (any 3-AP-free set with more than r elements works), but the source includes it (k, r ≥ 2). Scratch files are in /workspace/review/ (equiv2.lean, full_check2.lean).
